--[[
	PropertiesTabs  -  the Properties panel's second view, one section at a time under tabs. A header
	button switches between List (the scrolling list of type sections, with search) and Tabs: one
	type's sections as wrapping chips with the chosen section alone underneath, sliding in from the
	side. The header's two arrows (or the wheel over the chips or arrows) step to the previous / next
	section, on into the neighbouring type and round from the last to the first. With several types
	selected, a row of type chips sits above.
	PropertiesTabs.create(W, panel, parts) -> tabs
	  parts = { header, searchWrap, searchBox, scroll, top, scrollbar }   top = y under the header;
	    scrollbar = { thickness, gap } from PropertiesShell (nil in Classic)
	  tabs.CollapseProbe      add it LAST to the header arrow's item list: the arrow hides and shows
	                          it with the list, which is how this view follows a collapse
	  tabs.Host               the ScrollingFrame the pages sit in
	  tabs.attach()           once every type section exists under `scroll`
	  tabs.bindStore(plugin)  restores the saved view (setting PropsViewMode), then saves changes
	  tabs.setMode("list" | "tabs")
	  tabs.step(direction)    the header arrows: -1 the previous section, 1 the next
	Type sections are `scroll`'s W.makeSection children (`Header/Title` + `Body`). LIVE list frames
	change through Pages alone, on a type's first opening; the list's Visible flags (SelectionHandler)
	decide which get a chip. In Tabs PanelFit sets the panel's height; List's comes back on return.
	Refreshed by a type or section's Visible / Title, the open section resizing, the panel resizing
	and theme changes.
	Cross-file: W.makeDropdown switches off its ScrollingFrame ancestor's ScrollingEnabled while the
	cursor rests on it. Host is that ancestor, and every page change switches it back on, because a
	dropdown can leave with its page.
]]

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local C = require(script.Parent.Constants)
local TypeScale = require(script.Parent.TypeScale)
local ChipRow = require(script.ChipRow)
local Pages = require(script.Pages)
local PanelFit = require(script.PanelFit)
local T = C.T

local PropertiesTabs = {}

-- Between the type chips and the section chips.
local ROW_GAP = 8
-- Between the chips and the page, the divider in its middle; Classic has no divider and less gap.
local PAGE_GAP = 12
local CLASSIC_PAGE_GAP = 4
local PAGE_BOTTOM = 4
local MIN_PAGE_HEIGHT = 40
local SCREEN_MARGIN = 8
-- The panel grows to fit a section up to this height until its edge is dragged; past it, it scrolls.
local MAX_GROWN_HEIGHT = C.LAYOUT.PropsHeight
-- The header's step arrows: each one's width, and the first's place from the header's right edge.
local ARROW_WIDTH = 18
local ARROWS_RIGHT = 100
local ARROW_DIMMED = 0.65
-- Chips roomier than a tool deck's, by the theme's row height. Classic keeps the deck's.
local CHIP_PADDING = 16
local CHIP_GAP = 6
local WHEEL_COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 0.12
local MODE_SETTING = "PropsViewMode"
-- QOLSearch restores the list 0.05 s after the search text changes; adoption waits for it.
local SEARCH_SETTLE_SECONDS = 0.12

local function contains(guiObject, point)
	local origin = guiObject.AbsolutePosition
	local size = guiObject.AbsoluteSize
	return point.X >= origin.X and point.Y >= origin.Y and point.X <= origin.X + size.X and point.Y <= origin.Y + size.Y
end

function PropertiesTabs.create(W, panel, parts)
	local scroll = parts.scroll
	local mode = "list"
	local collapsed = false
	local switching = false
	local store = nil
	local types = {}
	local typesByKey = {}
	local activeType = nil
	local listHeight = panel.Size.Y.Offset
	local pageHeight = MIN_PAGE_HEIGHT
	local chipsBottom = 0
	local lastWheel = 0

	local area = Instance.new("Frame")
	area.Name = "TabsView"
	area.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	area.Visible = false
	area.Parent = panel

	-- Scrolls so a section taller than the screen is reachable, and dropdowns find it as their ancestor.
	local host = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame")
	host.Name = "Pages"
	host.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	host.BorderSizePixel = 0
	host.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	host.ScrollingDirection = Enum.ScrollingDirection.Y
	host.ScrollBarThickness = 3
	host.ScrollBarImageColor3 = T.ScrollBar
	host.Parent = area
	table.insert(W.getThemed().scrollbars, host)
	-- As the list's (PropertiesShell): reaches into the right padding so a field's outline is not clipped.
	local hostReach = 0
	if parts.scrollbar then
		hostReach = parts.scrollbar.gap + parts.scrollbar.thickness
		host.ScrollBarThickness = parts.scrollbar.thickness
		host.VerticalScrollBarInset = Enum.ScrollBarInset.Always
		W.addPadding(host, 0, parts.scrollbar.gap, 0, 0)
	end

	local divider = Instance.new("Frame")
	divider.Name = "Divider"
	divider.BorderSizePixel = 0
	divider.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 1)
	divider.Visible = not C.MODE.Structure.Classic
	W.paint(divider, "BackgroundColor3", "Divider")
	divider.Parent = area
	local pageGap = C.MODE.Structure.Classic and CLASSIC_PAGE_GAP or PAGE_GAP

	local function makeArrow(name, glyph, fromRight)
		local arrow = Instance.new("TextButton")
		arrow.Name = name
		arrow.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		arrow.AutoButtonColor = false
		arrow.Font = T.Font
		arrow.TextSize = 11
		arrow.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		arrow.Text = glyph
		-- Drawn like the header's collapse chevron beside them.
		if not C.MODE.Structure.Classic then
			TypeScale.style(arrow, "Chevron")
		end
		arrow.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
		arrow.Position = UDim2.new(1, -fromRight, 0, 0)
		arrow.Size = UDim2.new(0, ARROW_WIDTH, 1, 0)
		arrow.ZIndex = 3
		arrow.Visible = false
		arrow.Parent = parts.header
		arrow.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
			if W.pointerBlocked(arrow) then return end
			arrow.TextColor3 = T.Gold
		end)
		arrow.MouseLeave:Connect(function() arrow.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold end)
		return arrow
	end
	local previousArrow = makeArrow("PreviousSection", "\u{2039}", ARROWS_RIGHT + ARROW_WIDTH)
	local nextArrow = makeArrow("NextSection", "\u{203A}", ARROWS_RIGHT)

	local probe = Instance.new("Frame")
	probe.Name = "CollapseProbe"
	probe.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	probe.Size = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	probe.Parent = panel

	local viewButton = Instance.new("TextButton")
	viewButton.Name = "ViewMode"
	viewButton.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	viewButton.Font = T.Font
	viewButton.TextSize = 9
	viewButton.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
	viewButton.Text = "List"
	viewButton.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
	viewButton.Position = UDim2.new(1, -54, 0, 0)
	viewButton.Size = UDim2.new(0, 44, 1, 0)
	viewButton.ZIndex = 3
	viewButton.Parent = parts.header

	local metrics = {
		top = 0,
		padding = 0,
		pageBottom = PAGE_BOTTOM,
		minPage = MIN_PAGE_HEIGHT,
		screenMargin = SCREEN_MARGIN,
		ceiling = MAX_GROWN_HEIGHT,
	}
	W.layEach(area, function()
		metrics.top = W.measure(parts.top)
		metrics.padding = C.LAYOUT.PanelPad * 2
		area.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, metrics.top)
		area.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -metrics.top)
	end)
	local fit = PanelFit.new(W, panel, host, metrics)

	local function applyHeight(animate)
		if mode ~= "tabs" or collapsed then return end
		fit:apply(chipsBottom, pageHeight, animate)
	end

	local typeRow
	local sectionRow

	local refreshArrows

	-- Stacks the chip rows, divider and page host for the panel's width, then resizes the panel.
	local function relayout(animate)
		local width = panel.Size.X.Offset - metrics.padding
		local y = 0
		if typeRow.frame.Visible then
			typeRow.frame.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
			y = typeRow:layout(width) + ROW_GAP
		end
		sectionRow.frame.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, y)
		y += sectionRow:layout(width)
		divider.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, y + pageGap / 2)
		y += pageGap
		chipsBottom = y
		host.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, y)
		host.Size = UDim2.new(1, hostReach, 1, -y)
		refreshArrows()
		applyHeight(animate)
	end

	local pages
	local refreshSections

	pages = Pages.new(W, host, {
		onHeight = function(height)
			pageHeight = height
			applyHeight(true)
		end,
		onShownChanged = function(typeKey)
			if mode == "tabs" and activeType and activeType.key == typeKey then refreshSections() end
		end,
	})

	-- Pages are ordered by type, then by section, which gives a slide its direction.
	local function rankOf(page)
		return typesByKey[page.typeKey].rank * 1000 + page.index
	end

	-- stepDirection: a step that wraps round keeps sliding its way instead of following page order.
	local function openPage(page, animate, stepDirection)
		local direction = 1
		local current = pages.active
		if page and current and rankOf(page) < rankOf(current) then direction = -1 end
		if stepDirection then direction = stepDirection end
		host.CanvasPosition = Vector2.new(0, 0)
		-- A dropdown that left with its page never saw the cursor leave it.
		host.ScrollingEnabled = true
		pages:open(page, direction, animate)
		refreshArrows()
		if page then
			typesByKey[page.typeKey].lastKey = page.key
			sectionRow:setActive(page.key)
			return
		end
		sectionRow:setActive(nil)
		pageHeight = MIN_PAGE_HEIGHT
		applyHeight(animate)
	end

	local function shownTypes()
		local shown = {}
		for _, entry in ipairs(types) do
			if entry.frame.Visible then table.insert(shown, entry) end
		end
		return shown
	end

	-- Fills the active type's section chips; returns its shown pages.
	local function fillSectionChips()
		local shown = {}
		if activeType then shown = pages:shown(activeType.key) end
		local chips = {}
		for _, page in ipairs(shown) do
			table.insert(chips, { key = page.key, text = page.title })
		end
		sectionRow:setChips(chips)
		return shown
	end

	-- A section of the active type was shown or hidden: the open page changes only if it went away.
	function refreshSections()
		local shown = fillSectionChips()
		local current = pages.active
		if current and table.find(shown, current) then
			sectionRow:setActive(current.key)
		else
			openPage(shown[1], false)
		end
		relayout(false)
	end

	-- Opens `entry`'s sections, adopting them on first use. which: "remembered", "first" or "last".
	local function openType(entry, which, animate, stepDirection)
		activeType = entry
		if not entry then
			typeRow:setActive(nil)
			fillSectionChips()
			openPage(nil, false)
			relayout(false)
			return
		end
		typeRow:setActive(entry.key)
		pages:adopt(entry.key, entry.body)
		local shown = fillSectionChips()
		local target = shown[1]
		if which == "last" then
			target = shown[#shown]
		elseif which == "remembered" then
			for _, page in ipairs(shown) do
				if page.key == entry.lastKey then target = page end
			end
		end
		openPage(target, animate, stepDirection)
		relayout(animate)
	end

	local function refreshTypes()
		local shown = shownTypes()
		local chips = {}
		for _, entry in ipairs(shown) do
			table.insert(chips, { key = entry.key, text = entry.title.Text })
		end
		typeRow:setChips(chips)
		typeRow.frame.Visible = #shown > 1
		if mode ~= "tabs" then return end
		if not activeType or not activeType.frame.Visible then
			openType(shown[1], "remembered", false)
		else
			typeRow:setActive(activeType.key)
			relayout(false)
		end
	end

	-- What lies `step` from the open page: a page of the active type, else the next type on. Ends wrap
	-- round; nil, nil when there is nowhere to go.
	local function neighbourOf(step)
		if not activeType then return nil, nil end
		local shown = pages:shown(activeType.key)
		local index = table.find(shown, pages.active) or 0
		local page = shown[index + step]
		if page then return page, nil end

		local shownList = shownTypes()
		local typeAt = table.find(shownList, activeType)
		if typeAt and #shownList > 1 then
			return nil, shownList[(typeAt + step - 1) % #shownList + 1]
		end

		if #shown < 2 then return nil, nil end
		if step > 0 then return shown[1], nil end
		return shown[#shown], nil
	end

	local function stepSection(step)
		local page, entry = neighbourOf(step)
		if page then
			openPage(page, true, step)
		elseif entry and step > 0 then
			openType(entry, "first", true, step)
		elseif entry then
			openType(entry, "last", true, step)
		end
	end

	function refreshArrows()
		local previousPage, previousType = neighbourOf(-1)
		local nextPage, nextType = neighbourOf(1)
		previousArrow.TextTransparency = (previousPage or previousType) and 0 or ARROW_DIMMED
		nextArrow.TextTransparency = (nextPage or nextType) and 0 or ARROW_DIMMED
	end

	-- The chips' height follows the row height; the theme's repaint lays them out again.
	local chipMetrics = nil
	if not C.MODE.Structure.Classic then
		chipMetrics = { Height = 0, Padding = CHIP_PADDING, Gap = CHIP_GAP, Justify = true }
		W.layEach(area, function()
			chipMetrics.Height = C.LAYOUT.Row - 4
		end)
	end
	typeRow = ChipRow.new(W, area, function(key)
		local entry = typesByKey[key]
		if entry and entry ~= activeType then openType(entry, "remembered", true) end
	end, chipMetrics)
	typeRow.frame.Name = "TypeChips"
	typeRow.frame.Visible = false
	sectionRow = ChipRow.new(W, area, function(key)
		if not activeType then return end
		for _, page in ipairs(pages:shown(activeType.key)) do
			if page.key == key then openPage(page, true) end
		end
	end, chipMetrics)
	sectionRow.frame.Name = "SectionChips"

	local function applyVisibility()
		area.Visible = mode == "tabs" and not collapsed
		viewButton.Visible = not collapsed
		previousArrow.Visible = area.Visible
		nextArrow.Visible = area.Visible
		if mode == "tabs" then
			scroll.Visible = false
			parts.searchWrap.Visible = false
		elseif not collapsed then
			scroll.Visible = true
			parts.searchWrap.Visible = true
		end
		viewButton.Text = mode == "tabs" and "Tabs" or "List"
	end

	-- Whether another top-level frame (a floating editor, an open dropdown) covers the panel at `point`.
	local function coveredAt(point)
		local screenGui = panel.Parent
		if not screenGui then return false end
		local pastPanel = false
		for _, sibling in ipairs(screenGui:GetChildren()) do
			if sibling == panel then
				pastPanel = true
			elseif sibling:IsA("GuiObject") and sibling.Visible then
				local above = sibling.ZIndex > panel.ZIndex or (sibling.ZIndex == panel.ZIndex and pastPanel)
				if above and contains(sibling, point) then return true end
			end
		end
		return false
	end

	local tabs = {}

	function tabs.setMode(nextMode)
		if nextMode == mode or collapsed or switching then return end
		switching = true
		if nextMode == "tabs" then
			if parts.searchBox.Text ~= "" then
				parts.searchBox.Text = ""
				task.wait(SEARCH_SETTLE_SECONDS)
			end
			listHeight = W.restingSize(panel).Y.Offset
			fit:enter()
			mode = "tabs"
			applyVisibility()
			activeType = nil
			refreshTypes()
		else
			mode = "list"
			pages:release()
			activeType = nil
			applyVisibility()
			fit:leave(listHeight)
		end
		switching = false
		if store then pcall(function() store:SetSetting(MODE_SETTING, mode) end) end
	end

	function tabs.attach()
		for _, frame in ipairs(scroll:GetChildren()) do
			local header = frame:IsA("Frame") and frame:FindFirstChild("Header")
			local title = header and header:FindFirstChild("Title")
			local body = frame:FindFirstChild("Body")
			if title and body then
				-- lastKey: the section last open in this type. rank: its place in type order.
				local entry = { key = frame.Name, frame = frame, body = body, title = title, lastKey = nil, rank = 0 }
				table.insert(types, entry)
				typesByKey[entry.key] = entry
				frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(refreshTypes)
				title:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Text"):Connect(refreshTypes)
			end
		end
		table.sort(types, function(a, b) return a.frame.LayoutOrder < b.frame.LayoutOrder end)
		for index, entry in ipairs(types) do
			entry.rank = index
		end
		refreshTypes()
	end

	function tabs.bindStore(pluginRef)
		store = pluginRef
		local okMode, savedMode = pcall(function() return pluginRef:GetSetting(MODE_SETTING) end)
		if okMode and savedMode == "tabs" then task.defer(tabs.setMode, "tabs") end
	end

	function tabs.step(direction)
		if mode ~= "tabs" or collapsed then return end
		stepSection(direction)
	end

	viewButton.Activated:Connect(function()
		tabs.setMode(mode == "tabs" and "list" or "tabs")
	end)
	previousArrow.Activated:Connect(function() stepSection(-1) end)
	nextArrow.Activated:Connect(function() stepSection(1) end)

	probe:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(function()
		collapsed = not probe.Visible
		applyVisibility()
	end)

	-- An outside resize re-wraps the chips and refits the panel; a height set by hand becomes the ceiling.
	panel:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Size"):Connect(function()
		if mode ~= "tabs" or collapsed then return end
		if fit:resized() then return end
		relayout(false)
	end)

	-- The end of a resize by hand: the panel returns to the height of its section.
	table.insert(W.getUISConnections(), UserInputService.InputEnded:Connect(function(input)
		if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then return end
		if mode ~= "tabs" or collapsed then return end
		if fit:released() then relayout(true) end
	end))

	table.insert(W.getUISConnections(), UserInputService.InputChanged:Connect(function(input)
		if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseWheel then return end
		if mode ~= "tabs" or collapsed or not panel.Visible or not activeType then return end
		-- Only over the chips or arrows: over the page the wheel scrolls a tall section or cycles a dropdown.
		local mouse = UserInputService:GetMouseLocation()
		local overChips = contains(sectionRow.frame, mouse) or (typeRow.frame.Visible and contains(typeRow.frame, mouse))
		if not overChips and not contains(previousArrow, mouse) and not contains(nextArrow, mouse) then return end
		if coveredAt(mouse) then return end
		local now = os.clock()
		if now - lastWheel < WHEEL_COOLDOWN_SECONDS then return end
		lastWheel = now
		if input.Position.Z < 0 then
			stepSection(1)
		else
			stepSection(-1)
		end
	end))

	table.insert(W.getThemed().repaints, function()
		viewButton.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		previousArrow.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		nextArrow.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		typeRow:repaint()
		sectionRow:repaint()
		if mode == "tabs" and not collapsed then relayout(false) end
	end)

	tabs.CollapseProbe = probe
	tabs.Host = host
	return tabs
end

return PropertiesTabs

--[[
	ChipRow  -  a strip of the tool deck's tab chips that wraps onto further lines. Chips are placed by
	hand from measured text widths, so the strip's height is known at layout: the Properties tabs size
	the panel from it in the same step.
	ChipRow.new(W, parent, onPick, metrics) -> row; onPick(key) runs on a click
	  metrics                    optional { Height, Padding, Gap, Justify } instead of W.chipMetrics();
	                             Justify stretches every line but the last to the full width
	  .frame                     the strip; the owner positions it, :layout sets its height
	  :setChips(list)            list = { { key = , text = }, ... } in display order
	  :setActive(key)            lights that chip
	  :layout(width) -> height   places the chips in lines no wider than `width` (view units)
	  :repaint()                 theme colours
	Chips are W.makeChip buttons, reused and never destroyed: makeChip registers each chip's stroke
	with the themed list for the life of the UI.
]]

local ChipRow = {}
ChipRow.__index = ChipRow

function ChipRow.new(W, parent, onPick, metrics)
	local self = setmetatable({}, ChipRow)

	local frame = Instance.new("Frame")
	frame.Name = "Chips"
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	frame.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0)
	frame.Parent = parent

	self.frame = frame
	self._W = W
	self._metrics = metrics
	self._onPick = onPick
	self._buttons = {}
	self._chips = {}
	self._activeKey = nil
	return self
end

function ChipRow:_button(index)
	local button = self._buttons[index]
	if button then return button end
	button = self._W.makeChip("Chip" .. index, self.frame, "")
	button.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.None
	if self._metrics then
		-- makeChip rounded the chip for the deck's height.
		local corner = button:FindFirstChildOfClass("UICorner")
		if corner then
			self._W.lay(corner, "CornerRadius", function()
				return UDim.new(0, self._metrics.Height / 2)
			end)
		end
	end
	button.Activated:Connect(function()
		local chip = self._chips[index]
		if chip then self._onPick(chip.key) end
	end)
	self._buttons[index] = button
	return button
end

function ChipRow:setChips(list)
	self._chips = list
	for index, chip in ipairs(list) do
		local button = self:_button(index)
		button.Text = chip.text
		button.Visible = true
	end
	for index = #list + 1, #self._buttons do
		self._buttons[index].Visible = false
	end
	self:repaint()
end

function ChipRow:setActive(key)
	self._activeKey = key
	self:repaint()
end

function ChipRow:repaint()
	for index, chip in ipairs(self._chips) do
		self._W.paintChip(self._buttons[index], chip.key == self._activeKey)
	end
end

function ChipRow:layout(width)
	local metrics = self._metrics or self._W.chipMetrics()

	-- Chips at their text's width, broken into lines no wider than `width`.
	local lines = {}
	local line = { used = 0 }
	for index, chip in ipairs(self._chips) do
		local button = self._buttons[index]
		local textWidth = self._W.chipTextWidth(button, chip.text)
		local chipWidth = math.min(math.ceil(textWidth) + metrics.Padding, width)
		if #line > 0 and line.used + metrics.Gap + chipWidth > width then
			table.insert(lines, line)
			line = { used = 0 }
		end
		if #line > 0 then
			line.used += metrics.Gap
		end
		table.insert(line, { button = button, width = chipWidth })
		line.used += chipWidth
	end
	if #line > 0 then
		table.insert(lines, line)
	end

	local y = 0
	for lineIndex, entries in ipairs(lines) do
		local spare = 0
		if metrics.Justify and lineIndex < #lines then
			spare = (width - entries.used) / #entries
		end
		local x = 0
		for _, entry in ipairs(entries) do
			local left = math.floor(x + 0.5)
			local right = math.floor(x + entry.width + spare + 0.5)
			entry.button.Position = UDim2.new(0, left, 0, y)
			entry.button.Size = UDim2.new(0, right - left, 0, metrics.Height)
			x += entry.width + spare + metrics.Gap
		end
		y += metrics.Height + metrics.Gap
	end

	local height = 0
	if #lines > 0 then height = y - metrics.Gap end
	self.frame.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, height)
	return height
end

return ChipRow

--[[
	Pages  -  the section pages of the Properties tabs view. Each child of a type's list Body (its
	sections, and blocks such as the Blender box) rides in a `Page` holder, one page showing at a
	time, sliding in from the side. The frames are the LIVE ones the list uses: adopt() takes them out
	of their Body and release() puts them back, so every ref in UI.<Type> works in both views.
	adopt() opens a section's Body and hides its header's Arrow and Toggle; release() restores them.
	The list's stored collapse state is not touched.
	Pages.new(W, host, callbacks) -> pages
	  callbacks.onHeight(height)          the open page's height in view units, on open and when measured
	  callbacks.onShownChanged(typeKey)   the list's owner showed or hid a section of that type
	  .active                             the open page or nil (read only)
	  :adopt(typeKey, body)               no-op for a type already adopted
	  :release()
	  :shown(typeKey) -> { page, ... }    pages whose section is visible, in section order
	  :open(page, direction, animate)     1 slides in from the right, -1 from the left; nil closes
	  page = { typeKey, key, title, index, ... }   index = place among its type's pages
	Cross-file: a frame with `Header/Toggle` and `Body` is a W.makeSection section.
]]

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local Pages = {}
Pages.__index = Pages

local ORIGIN = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)

-- Arrow, Body and Toggle of a W.makeSection section; nil for any other frame.
local function sectionParts(frame)
	local header = frame:FindFirstChild("Header")
	local body = frame:FindFirstChild("Body")
	local toggle = header and header:FindFirstChild("Toggle")
	if not body or not toggle then return nil, nil, nil end
	return header:FindFirstChild("Arrow"), body, toggle
end

local function titleOf(frame)
	local header = frame:FindFirstChild("Header")
	local title = header and header:FindFirstChild("Title")
	if title and title:IsA("TextLabel") then return title.Text end
	local label = frame:FindFirstChild("Label", true)
	if label and label:IsA("TextLabel") then return label.Text end
	return frame.Name
end

function Pages.new(W, host, callbacks)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Pages)
	self._W = W
	self._host = host
	self._callbacks = callbacks
	self._types = {}
	self._slides = {}
	self.active = nil
	return self
end

function Pages:_screenScale()
	local screenGui = self._host:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("ScreenGui")
	local uiScale = screenGui and screenGui:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
	return uiScale and uiScale.Scale or 1
end

-- Reads the open page's height. A hidden page is not measured: its layout may be stale.
function Pages:_measure(page)
	if page ~= self.active then return end
	local height = page.frame.AbsoluteSize.Y / self:_screenScale()
	if height < 1 then return end
	if page.height and math.abs(height - page.height) < 0.5 then return end
	page.height = height
	self._callbacks.onHeight(height)
end

function Pages:_makePage(typeKey, frame)
	local holder = Instance.new("Frame")
	holder.Name = "Page"
	holder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	holder.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0)
	holder.Visible = false
	holder.Parent = self._host

	local arrow, body, toggle = sectionParts(frame)
	local page = {
		typeKey = typeKey,
		key = frame.Name,
		title = titleOf(frame),
		index = 0,
		frame = frame,
		holder = holder,
		arrow = arrow,
		body = body,
		toggle = toggle,
		bodyWasOpen = body ~= nil and body.Visible,
		height = nil,
		connections = {},
	}

	if body then
		body.Visible = true
		toggle.Visible = false
		if arrow then arrow.Visible = false end
	end
	frame.Parent = holder

	table.insert(page.connections, frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(function()
		self._callbacks.onShownChanged(typeKey)
	end))
	table.insert(page.connections, frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(function()
		self:_measure(page)
	end))
	return page
end

-- Moves every GuiObject child of `body` (LIVE list frames) into a page holder.
function Pages:adopt(typeKey, body)
	if self._types[typeKey] then return end
	local entry = { body = body, pages = {} }
	self._types[typeKey] = entry
	for _, child in ipairs(body:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("GuiObject") then
			table.insert(entry.pages, self:_makePage(typeKey, child))
		end
	end
	table.sort(entry.pages, function(a, b) return a.frame.LayoutOrder < b.frame.LayoutOrder end)
	for index, page in ipairs(entry.pages) do
		page.index = index
	end
end

-- Returns every adopted frame to its list Body as it was, and drops the holders.
function Pages:release()
	self:_finishSlides()
	for _, entry in pairs(self._types) do
		for _, page in ipairs(entry.pages) do
			for _, connection in ipairs(page.connections) do
				connection:Disconnect()
			end
			if page.body then
				page.body.Visible = page.bodyWasOpen
				page.toggle.Visible = true
				if page.arrow then page.arrow.Visible = true end
			end
			page.frame.Parent = entry.body
			page.holder:Destroy()
		end
	end
	self._types = {}
	self.active = nil
end

function Pages:shown(typeKey)
	local shown = {}
	local entry = self._types[typeKey]
	if not entry then return shown end
	for _, page in ipairs(entry.pages) do
		if page.frame.Visible then table.insert(shown, page) end
	end
	return shown
end

-- Ends any running slide: every holder back at the origin, a leaving page hidden.
function Pages:_finishSlides()
	for _, slide in ipairs(self._slides) do
		slide.tween:Cancel()
		slide.holder.Position = ORIGIN
		if slide.leaving then slide.holder.Visible = false end
	end
	self._slides = {}
end

function Pages:_slide(holder, target, leaving)
	local tween = TweenService:Create(holder, self._W.deckSlide(), { Position = target })
	table.insert(self._slides, { tween = tween, holder = holder, leaving = leaving })
	if leaving then
		tween.Completed:Connect(function(playbackState)
			if playbackState ~= Enum.PlaybackState.Completed then return end
			holder.Visible = false
			holder.Position = ORIGIN
		end)
	end
	tween:Play()
end

function Pages:open(page, direction, animate)
	local outgoing = self.active
	if outgoing == page then return end
	self:_finishSlides()
	self.active = page

	local slides = animate and outgoing ~= nil and page ~= nil
	if outgoing then
		if slides then
			self:_slide(outgoing.holder, UDim2.new(-direction, 0, 0, 0), true)
		else
			outgoing.holder.Visible = false
		end
	end
	if not page then return end

	page.holder.Visible = true
	if slides then
		page.holder.Position = UDim2.new(direction, 0, 0, 0)
		self:_slide(page.holder, ORIGIN, false)
	else
		page.holder.Position = ORIGIN
	end

	if page.height then self._callbacks.onHeight(page.height) end
	-- Read once here too: the AbsoluteSize signal stays silent when the hidden size was already right.
	task.spawn(function()
		task.wait()
		self:_measure(page)
	end)
end

return Pages

--[[
	PanelFit  -  the Properties panel's height while its Tabs view is open: as tall as the chips and
	the open section, up to a ceiling; a taller section scrolls inside the host.
	PanelFit.new(W, panel, host, metrics) -> fit
	  metrics = { top (y under the header), padding (UIPadding, both edges), pageBottom (air under the
	    last row), minPage (least room kept for a section), screenMargin (kept clear above the screen's
	    bottom), ceiling (the tallest it fits to until the user says otherwise) }
	  fit:enter()                                  the view opens: the ceiling goes back to metrics.ceiling
	  fit:leave(height)                            the view closes: the panel gets `height` at once
	  fit:apply(chipsBottom, pageHeight, animate)  fits the panel to the chips' bottom plus the section
	  fit:resized() -> boolean                     the Size changed; true when this module wrote it
	  fit:released() -> boolean                    mouse up; true when it ended a resize by hand
	The ceiling is the user's: dragging the top or bottom edge sets it until the view opens again, and
	during that drag the panel is left to the hand. Any other height from outside is fitted over.
	Mutates the LIVE panel's Size and host.CanvasSize. A panel pushed by one in front (PanelPush) keeps
	the height it was pushed to.
	Cross-file: Widgets.makeResizable names the edge under a drag through W.resizingAxis(panel), and
	writes the drag's starting height on every move of a width drag.
]]

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local PanelFit = {}
PanelFit.__index = PanelFit

function PanelFit.new(W, panel, host, metrics)
	local self = setmetatable({}, PanelFit)
	self.W = W
	self.panel = panel
	self.host = host
	self.metrics = metrics
	self.ceiling = metrics.ceiling
	-- The height this module last gave the panel, or the one a drag by hand holds it at.
	self.held = 0
	self.byHand = false
	self.tween = nil
	self.writing = false
	-- Counts the fits asked for, so one can tell that another ran inside it.
	self.asked = 0
	return self
end

function PanelFit:enter()
	self.ceiling = self.metrics.ceiling
	self.held = 0
	self.byHand = false
end

function PanelFit:_stopTween()
	local running = self.tween
	self.tween = nil
	if running then
		running:Cancel()
	end
end

function PanelFit:leave(height)
	self:_stopTween()
	self.writing = false
	self.byHand = false
	self.panel.Size = UDim2.new(0, self.panel.Size.X.Offset, 0, height)
end

-- The tallest the panel may get: down to the bottom of the screen from where it sits.
function PanelFit:_room(chipsBottom)
	local panel = self.panel
	local metrics = self.metrics
	local screenGui = panel:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("ScreenGui")
	if not screenGui then
		return math.huge
	end
	local uiScale = screenGui:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
	local scale = 1
	if uiScale then
		scale = uiScale.Scale
	end
	local top = (panel.AbsolutePosition.Y - screenGui.AbsolutePosition.Y) / scale
	local room = screenGui.AbsoluteSize.Y / scale - top - metrics.screenMargin
	return math.max(room, metrics.padding + metrics.top + chipsBottom + metrics.minPage)
end

function PanelFit:apply(chipsBottom, pageHeight, animate)
	local panel = self.panel
	local metrics = self.metrics
	local wanted = metrics.padding + metrics.top + chipsBottom + pageHeight + metrics.pageBottom
	-- Reading the screen lays the page out, and a section measured for the first time fits the panel
	-- from inside this call with its real height: that fit stands and this earlier one is dropped.
	self.asked += 1
	local asked = self.asked
	local room = self:_room(chipsBottom)
	local pushed = self.W.panelPushed(panel)
	if self.asked ~= asked then
		return
	end
	local held = pushed or self.byHand
	if not held then
		self.held = math.min(wanted, self.ceiling, room)
	end

	-- The section scrolls when the panel cannot hold it.
	local showing = self.held
	if pushed then
		showing = panel.Size.Y.Offset
	end
	local canvasHeight = 0
	if wanted - showing > 1 then
		canvasHeight = pageHeight
	end
	self.host.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, canvasHeight)
	if held then
		return
	end

	local size = UDim2.new(0, panel.Size.X.Offset, 0, self.held)
	self:_stopTween()
	self.writing = true
	if animate and panel.Visible then
		local tween = TweenService:Create(panel, self.W.deckSlide(), { Size = size })
		self.tween = tween
		tween.Completed:Connect(function()
			if self.tween ~= tween then
				return
			end
			self.tween = nil
			self.writing = false
		end)
		tween:Play()
	else
		panel.Size = size
		self.writing = false
	end
end

function PanelFit:resized()
	if self.writing then
		return true
	end
	local panel = self.panel
	local height = panel.Size.Y.Offset
	if height == self.held then
		return false
	end
	if self.W.resizingAxis(panel) == "y" then
		-- The edge under the user's hand: the panel is theirs until they let go.
		self.ceiling = height
		self.held = height
		self.byHand = true
	end
	return false
end

function PanelFit:released()
	if not self.byHand then
		return false
	end
	self.byHand = false
	return true
end

return PanelFit

--[[
	RandomizerPanel  -  Part-Icles V5 Randomizer System

	The Randomize modal: a tristate checkbox tree of randomizable properties (with Group axes and
	palette toggles) over a Roll / Apply / Cancel row. RandomizerWiring fills and wires it:
	  Open   -> QOL.snapshotItem per item
	  Roll   -> per item and property derive() + roll() + RandomizerWriter.write()
	  Apply  -> ChangeHistory waypoint, snapshots dropped
	  Cancel -> QOL.restoreSnapshots(snapshots), close
]]

local C = require(script.Parent.Constants)
local W = require(script.Parent.Widgets)
local TypeScale = require(script.Parent.TypeScale)
local PanelSizes = require(script.Parent.PanelSizes)
local T = C.T
local LAYOUT = C.LAYOUT

local RandomizerPanel = {}

-- refs: panel, sectionList, rollAllBtn, applyBtn, cancelBtn, headerCloseBtn (makeToolPanel's
-- Hd.Close). Every close path must go through wiring.cancel() to restore the previewed values.
local function buildClassic(sg)
	-- A modal in front of Properties, opaque (_opaquePanel); 220 px fits the longest property names.
	local panel = W.makeToolPanel(sg, "Randomize", 220, 400)
	panel:SetAttribute("_opaquePanel", true)
	panel:SetAttribute("_noSnap", true)
	panel.Visible = false -- the toolbar toggle shows it

	local refs = {panel = panel}

	local hd = panel:FindFirstChild("Hd")
	if hd then refs.headerCloseBtn = hd:FindFirstChild("Close") end

	-- RandomizerWiring.populateSections fills it.
	local sectionList = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame")
	sectionList.Name = "SectionList"
	sectionList.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	sectionList.BorderSizePixel = 0
	sectionList.Position = UDim2.new(0, 4, 0, 26)
	sectionList.Size = UDim2.new(1, -8, 1, -56)
	sectionList.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	sectionList.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
	sectionList.ScrollBarThickness = 2
	sectionList.ScrollBarImageColor3 = T.ScrollBar
	sectionList.Parent = panel
	W.addListLayout(sectionList, 4, Enum.FillDirection.Vertical)
	refs.sectionList = sectionList

	-- Shown until populateSections rebuilds the list (it destroys every TextLabel and Frame child).
	local placeholder = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	placeholder.Name = "Placeholder"
	placeholder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	placeholder.Text = "Loading…"
	placeholder.TextColor3 = T.DarkGold
	placeholder.Font = T.Font
	placeholder.TextSize = 8
	placeholder.TextWrapped = true
	placeholder.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Center
	placeholder.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 32)
	placeholder.Parent = sectionList

	local btnRow = Instance.new("Frame")
	btnRow.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	btnRow.Size = UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 22)
	btnRow.Position = UDim2.new(0, 4, 1, -26)
	btnRow.Parent = panel
	W.addListLayout(btnRow, 2, Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal)

	refs.rollAllBtn = W.makeButton("RandRoll", btnRow, "Roll", UDim2.new(1/3, -2, 1, 0))
	refs.rollAllBtn.LayoutOrder = 0
	refs.rollAllBtn.TextSize = 9
	refs.applyBtn = W.makeButton("RandApply", btnRow, "Apply", UDim2.new(1/3, -2, 1, 0), T.Gold)
	refs.applyBtn.LayoutOrder = 1
	refs.applyBtn.TextSize = 9
	refs.cancelBtn = W.makeButton("RandCancel", btnRow, "Cancel", UDim2.new(1/3, -2, 1, 0), T.DarkGold)
	refs.cancelBtn.LayoutOrder = 2
	refs.cancelBtn.TextSize = 9

	return refs
end

-- The same refs on the mode's tool shell: the list fills the body, the buttons sit under it.
local function buildModern(sg)
	local panel, chrome = W.makeToolShell(sg, "Randomize", PanelSizes.of("Randomizer"), PanelSizes.of("RandomizerHeight"))
	panel:SetAttribute("_opaquePanel", true)
	panel:SetAttribute("_noSnap", true)
	local body = chrome.body

	-- Every close path must reach wiring.cancel(), which restores the previewed values.
	local refs = { panel = panel, headerCloseBtn = chrome.close }

	-- RandomizerWiring.populateSections fills the list.
	local sectionList = W.makeLoadingList(body, "SectionList")
	W.lay(sectionList, "Size", function()
		return UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -(LAYOUT.Row + LAYOUT.RowGap))
	end)
	refs.sectionList = sectionList

	local buttons, buttonRow = W.makeButtonRow(body, "Buttons", {
		{ name = "RandRoll", text = "Roll" },
		{ name = "RandApply", text = "Apply", role = "TextHeading" },
		{ name = "RandCancel", text = "Cancel", role = "TextSecondary" },
	}, 0)
	buttonRow.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 1)
	buttonRow.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 1, 0)
	refs.rollAllBtn = buttons[1]
	refs.applyBtn = buttons[2]
	refs.cancelBtn = buttons[3]

	return refs
end

function RandomizerPanel.build(sg)
	if C.MODE.Structure.Classic then
		return buildClassic(sg)
	end
	return buildModern(sg)
end

return RandomizerPanel

--[[
	Relayout  -  live layout: what a builder takes from Constants.LAYOUT, Constants.MODE.Structure or
	the panel sizes is kept as a slot, a small function run again when the layout changes, so a mode,
	text size, metric or structure switch changes the UI in place instead of rebuilding it.
	UIBuilder:UpdateTheme runs every slot after Constants.refresh, before the colours and Skin.
	  Relayout.set(inst, property, compute)   inst[property] = compute(), now and at each run
	  Relayout.props(inst, compute)           compute() -> { property = value }: several at once
	  Relayout.each(inst, apply)              apply(inst), now and at each run, for what nothing else writes
	  Relayout.run()                          every slot again, in the order made
	  Relayout.reset()                        a new build starts with none
	  Relayout.swap(held) -> was              another build's slots in use (Widgets.buildAside)
	  Relayout.hold(inst, property)           the value there now counts as its slots' own, so a
	                                          builder's later write (a panel fitted to content) keeps them
	  Relayout.value(inst, property)          what inst's newest slot gives now (even one let go): the
	                                          default Reset Layout returns to; nil when none lays it
	A property slot gives a new value only while the property still holds the one it last gave: a
	change since (a user resize, a tween) stays. A newer slot on an instance takes the property over
	from older ones. A property Skin holds for a Custom layer (`_skinWas<Property>`, Skin.remember)
	takes the new value there, for Skin to give back when the layer goes. A slot goes once its
	instance is destroyed; a widget parked outside the tree keeps its slots.
]]

local Relayout = {}

local slots = {}
-- Instance -> its slots (strong, swept with `slots`).
local byInstance = {}
-- The slot count at which destroyed instances are next swept.
local sweepAt = 2048
-- True while run() walks the list: a sweep then would move the slots it has yet to reach.
local running = false

-- Destroy locks an instance's Parent at nil; a parked one (Parent set to nil) can still take it.
local function destroyed(inst)
	if inst.Parent ~= nil then
		return false
	end
	return not pcall(function()
		inst.Parent = nil
	end)
end

local function index(slot)
	local list = byInstance[slot.inst]
	if not list then
		list = {}
		byInstance[slot.inst] = list
	end
	table.insert(list, slot)
end

local function sweep()
	local kept = {}
	byInstance = {}
	for _, slot in ipairs(slots) do
		if not destroyed(slot.inst) then
			table.insert(kept, slot)
			index(slot)
		end
	end
	slots = kept
	sweepAt = math.max(2048, #slots * 2)
end

-- Gives a property its new value unless something changed it since the last one given; returns
-- whether it did.
local function give(inst, property, value, hasGiven, given)
	local held = "_skinWas" .. property
	local skinHolds = inst:GetAttribute(held) ~= nil
	local current = if skinHolds then inst:GetAttribute(held) else inst[property]
	if hasGiven and current ~= given then
		return false
	end
	if skinHolds then
		inst:SetAttribute(held, value)
	else
		inst[property] = value
	end
	return true
end

local function apply(slot)
	local inst = slot.inst
	if slot.apply then
		slot.apply(inst)
	elseif slot.property then
		local value = slot.compute()
		if give(inst, slot.property, value, slot.hasGiven, slot.given) then
			slot.hasGiven, slot.given = true, value
		else
			-- Changed by something else: the slot lets go of the property for good.
			slot.released = true
		end
	else
		slot.given = slot.given or {}
		slot.loose = slot.loose or {}
		for property, value in pairs(slot.compute()) do
			if not slot.loose[property] then
				local hasGiven = slot.given[property] ~= nil
				if give(inst, property, value, hasGiven, slot.given[property]) then
					slot.given[property] = value
				else
					slot.loose[property] = true
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

local function propertiesOf(slot)
	if slot.property then
		return { [slot.property] = true }
	end
	local given = {}
	for property in pairs(slot.given or {}) do
		given[property] = true
	end
	return given
end

-- The older slots on the new slot's instance let go of the properties it gives.
local function supersede(slot)
	local older = byInstance[slot.inst]
	if not older or slot.apply then
		return
	end
	local taken = propertiesOf(slot)
	for _, other in ipairs(older) do
		if other == slot then
			continue
		elseif other.property and taken[other.property] then
			other.released = true
		elseif other.property == nil and other.apply == nil then
			other.loose = other.loose or {}
			for property in pairs(taken) do
				other.loose[property] = true
			end
		end
	end
end

-- In the list before its first apply: slots an each slot makes as it runs come after it.
local function add(slot)
	table.insert(slots, slot)
	index(slot)
	apply(slot)
	supersede(slot)
	if not running and #slots >= sweepAt then
		sweep()
	end
end

function Relayout.set(inst, property, compute)
	add({ inst = inst, property = property, compute = compute })
	return inst
end

function Relayout.props(inst, compute)
	add({ inst = inst, compute = compute })
	return inst
end

function Relayout.each(inst, applyTo)
	add({ inst = inst, apply = applyTo })
	return inst
end

function Relayout.run()
	sweep()
	-- A slot that remakes its widget may make slots of its own: those ran as they were made.
	local count = #slots
	running = true
	for position = 1, count do
		local slot = slots[position]
		if not slot.released and not destroyed(slot.inst) then
			apply(slot)
		end
	end
	running = false
end

function Relayout.reset()
	slots = {}
	byInstance = {}
	sweepAt = 2048
end

-- Puts `held` (another build's slots, or nil) in use and returns the ones that were, so a build
-- kept apart (Widgets.buildAside) never gets the UI's relayouts.
function Relayout.swap(held)
	local was = { slots = slots, byInstance = byInstance, sweepAt = sweepAt }
	held = held or { slots = {}, byInstance = {}, sweepAt = 2048 }
	slots, byInstance, sweepAt = held.slots, held.byInstance, held.sweepAt
	return was
end

function Relayout.hold(inst, property)
	for _, slot in ipairs(byInstance[inst] or {}) do
		if slot.property == property and not slot.released then
			slot.hasGiven, slot.given = true, inst[property]
		elseif slot.property == nil and slot.apply == nil and slot.given and slot.given[property] ~= nil and not slot.loose[property] then
			slot.given[property] = inst[property]
		end
	end
end

function Relayout.value(inst, property)
	local list = byInstance[inst] or {}
	for position = #list, 1, -1 do
		local slot = list[position]
		if slot.property == property then
			return slot.compute()
		elseif slot.property == nil and slot.apply == nil then
			local value = slot.compute()[property]
			if value ~= nil then
				return value
			end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- How many slots there are, for the checks.
function Relayout.count()
	return #slots
end

return Relayout

--[[
	RenamePanel  -  the Rename popup (RenameTool wires it; Actions.RenameSelection opens it, key N):
	the pattern, the order, the numbering's Start / Step / Digits, a preview of the first names, the
	main tokens, and Cancel / Rename. One builder for every mode: the tool shell gives each mode its
	frame and the rows stack under it. The preview's rows always exist (blank when unused), so the
	popup fits itself to its rows in any mode and text size.
	  RenamePanel.build(sg) -> refs: RenamePanel, RenamePattern, RenameStart, RenameStep, RenameDigits,
	    RenamePreviewRows (labels, in order), RenameMore, RenameApply, RenameCancel,
	    setRenameOrderChanged(fn(text)), RenameTitleCount(count)
	The order choices are RenameTool.ORDERS (RenameTool requires nothing).
]]

local C = require(script.Parent.Constants)
local W = require(script.Parent.Widgets)
local TypeScale = require(script.Parent.TypeScale)
local PanelSizes = require(script.Parent.PanelSizes)
local RenameTool = require(script.Parent.Parent.Parent.RenameTool)
local LAYOUT = C.LAYOUT

local RenamePanel = {}

local ORDERS = RenameTool.ORDERS
local PREVIEW_ROWS = 3
local TOKENS = "$ name    * number    {a} letter"

-- A label in the theme's colour for its role, at the mode's text size for `typeRole`.
local function label(parent, name, text, colorRole, typeRole, order)
	local made = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	made.Name = name
	made.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	made.Text = text
	made.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	made.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd
	W.lay(made, "Size", function()
		return UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, LAYOUT.Row - 6)
	end)
	made.LayoutOrder = order or 0
	TypeScale.style(made, typeRole)
	W.paint(made, "TextColor3", colorRole)
	made.Parent = parent
	return made
end

-- One cell of the numbering row: a caption and a short field.
local function numberCell(row, name, caption, default, order)
	local cell = Instance.new("Frame")
	cell.Name = name .. "Cell"
	cell.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	W.lay(cell, "Size", function()
		return UDim2.new(1 / 3, -LAYOUT.RowGap * 2 / 3, 1, 0)
	end)
	cell.LayoutOrder = order
	cell.Parent = row
	local captionLabel = W.makeRowLabel(cell, caption, 0)
	captionLabel.Size = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, 0)
	TypeScale.style(captionLabel, "Caption")
	local box, field = W.makeTextField(cell, name, default, Enum.TextXAlignment.Center)
	field.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 0)
	field.Size = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, 0)
	return box
end

function RenamePanel.build(sg)
	-- The height fit() gave the panel from its rows: what a relayout keeps, until fit runs again.
	local fittedHeight = nil
	local panel, chrome = W.makeToolShell(sg, "Rename", PanelSizes.of("Rename"), function()
		return fittedHeight or PanelSizes.get().RenameHeight
	end)
	local refs = { RenamePanel = panel }

	local content = Instance.new("Frame")
	content.Name = "RenameContent"
	content.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	content.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, chrome.bodyTop)
	content.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -chrome.bodyTop)
	content.Parent = chrome.body
	W.addListLayout(content, "RowGap")

	refs.RenamePattern = W.makeTextField(content, "RenamePattern", "")
	refs.RenamePattern.PlaceholderText = "Shockwave_{n}"
	refs.RenamePattern.Parent.LayoutOrder = 1

	local orderRow = W.makeRowFrame(content, "RenameOrderRow", 2)
	local _, orderWrap, onOrderChanged = W.makeDropdown("RenameOrder", orderRow, ORDERS, ORDERS[1])
	orderWrap.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	orderWrap.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)
	refs.setRenameOrderChanged = onOrderChanged

	local numbers = W.makeRowFrame(content, "RenameNumbers", 3)
	W.addListLayout(numbers, "RowGap", Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal)
	refs.RenameStart = numberCell(numbers, "RenameStart", "Start", "1", 1)
	refs.RenameStep = numberCell(numbers, "RenameStep", "Step", "1", 2)
	refs.RenameDigits = numberCell(numbers, "RenameDigits", "Digits", "1", 3)

	local preview = Instance.new("Frame")
	preview.Name = "RenamePreview"
	preview.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	preview.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0)
	preview.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
	preview.LayoutOrder = 5
	preview.Parent = content
	W.addListLayout(preview, 0)
	refs.RenamePreviewRows = {}
	for index = 1, PREVIEW_ROWS do
		refs.RenamePreviewRows[index] = label(preview, "Preview" .. index, "", "TextPrimary", "Value", index)
	end
	refs.RenameMore = label(preview, "More", "", "TextLabel", "Caption", PREVIEW_ROWS + 1)

	label(content, "Tokens", TOKENS, "TextLabel", "Caption", 6)

	local buttons = W.makeButtonRow(content, "RenameButtons", {
		{ name = "RenameCancel", text = "Cancel" },
		{ name = "RenameApply", text = "Rename", role = "Success" },
	}, 7)
	refs.RenameCancel, refs.RenameApply = buttons[1], buttons[2]

	function refs.RenameTitleCount(count)
		chrome.title.Text = count == 1 and "Rename 1 item" or string.format("Rename %d items", count)
	end

	-- What the panel has beyond its rows (title bar, padding) plus the rows: its height.
	local layout = content:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIListLayout")
	local function fit()
		local scale = panel.AbsoluteSize.Y / math.max(panel.Size.Y.Offset, 1)
		if scale <= 0 then
			return
		end
		local around = panel.Size.Y.Offset - content.AbsoluteSize.Y / scale
		local wanted = math.ceil(around + layout.AbsoluteContentSize.Y / scale)
		if math.abs(wanted - panel.Size.Y.Offset) > 1 then
			fittedHeight = wanted
			panel.Size = UDim2.new(panel.Size.X.Scale, panel.Size.X.Offset, 0, wanted)
			-- The fit is the panel's own: its width still follows the layout.
			W.layHold(panel, "Size")
		end
	end
	layout:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteContentSize"):Connect(fit)
	task.defer(fit)
	return refs
end

return RenamePanel
